$comment: Advisories this build knowingly ships with, each with a reason and an expiry.
An advisory not listed here fails the gate. An entry past its expiry fails the
gate. An entry that no longer matches anything also fails the gate, so the list
cannot quietly rot into a permanent allowance.

why: Cubic-time decoding of malformed percent-encoded input (CVE-2026-45822): 0.2.2
spends 32 s on 400 malformed escapes. The fix is 0.5.0, and it cannot be installed
here. 0.3.0 onwards is ESM-only, and the only dependent is query-string 7.1.3, which
`require`s this package and calls the result; every expo-router 57 release pins
query-string ^7.1.3, and npm's own suggested fix is expo-router 5.1.11, four SDKs
back. An override to 0.5.0 would hand query-string a module namespace, not a function.
Path: apps/mobile -> expo-router -> query-string 7.1.3 -> decode-uri-component 0.2.2,
bundled into the mobile app. expo-router parses incoming links with its own
URLSearchParams-based fork, so the only caller that decodes is the vendored React
Navigation getStateFromPath it replaces; that is an argument about today's call graph,
not a control. The control is the fix itself: patches/decode-uri-component+0.2.2.patch
backports 0.5.0's single-pass decoder (upstream fa479da) and keeps 0.2.2's
`+`-to-space conversion, so nothing else about the 0.2 contract moves.
verify-dependency-patches checks the installed file's digest and decodes the
pathological input. npm audit matches on the version number, which a patch cannot
change, so the advisory still needs this entry.
GHSA-qr28-fpjm-wq7f is the quadratic-replacement advisory, and it covers every
published release including 0.5.0. The same single-pass decoder backport
removes that path too, so the patch is the control for both findings.
Owner: Iroha PDF maintainers.
Revisit when expo-router takes query-string 9.5 or later (which accepts
decode-uri-component 0.5) or stops depending on it. Remove the patch and this entry
together.
Prototype poisoning of the object mergeObject() returns. It reaches this project
only through @expo/config while the Expo CLI reads the project's own app.json
at build time; no user-opened document and no untrusted remote input passes
through it. npm's suggested fix is Expo 53, three SDKs back, which is not a fix.
Revisit when @expo/config moves to a fixed deepmerge, or when Expo 58 lands.
AbortSignal cancellation bypass in a glob traversal. Every path is in Expo CLI,
@expo/config, metro and react-native-blob-util's Node-side tooling, walking the
repository during development and bundling — not a path derived from a document
a user opens. The fix is glob 14.0.2, but Expo 57 pins glob 13; npm's suggested
fix is Expo 53, three SDKs back.
Revisit when Expo moves to glob 14.0.2 or later.
CPU amplification in globparts matching, reached only through the same Expo
build tooling chain as glob above and over repository paths. Fixed in
minimatch 11.0.1, but glob 13 pins minimatch 10 and Expo 57 pins glob 13.
Revisit when Expo's glob moves to a minimatch 11.0.1 or later.
Memory exhaustion while validating oversized constrained collections. The only
consumer is @expo/cli at development time, validating its own configuration;
it is not bundled into the desktop or mobile application. The fix is zod 4.6.6,
and Expo CLI 57 pins zod 3.25, whose schema API is not source compatible.
Revisit when @expo/cli adopts zod 4.6.6 or later.
